clue.text: Court studies motion covering national compensation for losers

indicators.note: covering says the word for motion is laid over, and so placed before, the abbreviation for national

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them
dens are studies, rooms for private work
a motion is a bowel movement, informally poo

explanation.surface: A tennis court where players study the motion to award something to the losing side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a noun, a tennis or law court, but is the verb to woo. 'covering' puts N inside POO. The answer runs into 9 Down, SPOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden spoon is the booby prize, given in jest to whoever finishes last, as in the Six Nations rugby table.

clue.text: Working sustains power in tired arms

indicators.note: in places the pair inside the word for tired

parts.note: weary means tired

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for working sits below and so holds up the letter for power

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A worker's tired arms are kept going by sheer power.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, a piece that 'sustains' another sits beneath it, holding it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms in the sense of weapons; weaponry is the collective word for them.

clue.text: Aware of where you might see Gilbert in 14?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for alert and aware

definitions.text: where you might see Gilbert in 14?
definitions.meaning: Gilbert makes rugby balls, used in the Six Nations (14 Down)

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about spotting someone called Gilbert in a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert is not a person here but the rugby-ball maker whose name is printed on the balls used in the Six Nations championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the ball is an idiom for being alert and quick to understand.

clue.text: First female leader of Netherlands quits

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Netherlands

explanation.surface: The first woman to lead the Netherlands resigns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quits' looks like a verb, to resign, but is the adjective in 'we're quits'.
explanation.definitionFit: To be quits is to be square, with neither party owing the other anything.

clue.text: Clippers help to crush resistance, chasing ship around Channel Islands

indicators.note: chasing says the help group comes after the ship group
around says the ship abbreviation goes round the islands abbreviation

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

indicators.note: to crush something is to squeeze it, so the call for help is squeezed round the resistance letter

parts.note: SOS is the distress call asking for help
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Clipper ships being chased about the Channel Islands while help arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clippers' suggests sailing ships, which suits 'ship' and 'Channel', but means a cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Scissors are a tool for clipping, so they can be called clippers.

clue.text: Hound experts about Italy's religious offices

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog or hound

indicators.note: about says the experts go round the letter for Italy

parts.note: aces are experts
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Hounding experts over Italy's church posts.
explanation.definitionFit: A curacy is the office of a curate, an assistant priest, so curacies are church posts.

clue.text: Horseman, justice and unionist politician caught in downpour

indicators.note: caught in says the three letters are trapped inside the word for rain

parts.note: a shower is a fall of rain
J is the abbreviation for Justice, a judge's title
U stands for Unionist, as in Northern Irish party names
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A rider, a judge and a unionist MP all caught in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A showjumper is a rider who jumps horses over fences in competition.

clue.text: Selected bar featured in newspaper article

indicators.note: featured in says the bar letter appears within the article

parts.note: an op-ed is an opinion piece printed opposite the editorial page
a T is a bar shape, as in T-bar

explanation.surface: A bar picked for a write-up in the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to choose, so opted means chose.

clue.text: Globe enveloped by congealed icy liquid

indicators.note: enveloped by says the globe word is wrapped inside the word for congealed

parts.note: set means congealed or solidified
an orb is a globe

explanation.surface: A globe wrapped in something frozen and liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorbet is a water ice, frozen sweetened fruit juice, so an icy semi-liquid dessert.

clue.text: See 1
An imbecile in port

parts.note: a twerp is a silly person

explanation.surface: An idiot sitting in a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Antwerp is a major Belgian port city on the Scheldt.

clue.text: Love interrupts work schedule? It's emblematic of the French!

indicators.note: interrupts says the letter for love breaks into the schedule

parts.note: a roster is a rota of work shifts
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Romance getting in the way of a work timetable, as one might expect of the French.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gallic cockerel is the national emblem of France, worn on French rugby shirts.

clue.text: Retreating captain gives warning

indicators.note: retreating says the captain's name goes backwards

parts.note: Captain Nemo is the submarine commander in Jules Verne's novels

explanation.surface: A captain pulling back and issuing a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of what is to come, often a warning of trouble.

clue.text: Dutch jog awkwardly around bend beside European flag-bearer

indicators.note: around says the jumbled letters go round the bend letter
awkwardly says the letters of dutch jog are jumbled

parts.note: a U-bend, so U is a bend shape

explanation.surface: A Dutchman jogging clumsily round a corner next to a European carrying a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' jumbles DUTCH JOG and 'around' puts that round U; E is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A touch judge is the rugby official who raises a flag when the ball goes out of play.

clue.text: Sit in on sax playing competition

indicators.note: playing says the letters of sit in on sax are moved about

explanation.surface: Join in with saxophone playing at a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Six Nations is the annual rugby union tournament between England, France, Ireland, Italy, Scotland and Wales.

clue.text: Echo on radio confounded sound engineer, for instance

indicators.note: on says the echo letter is placed on the end of the jumble
confounded says the letters of radio are mixed up

parts.note: Echo is E in the radio phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An echo on the radio baffles a sound engineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadie is a member of a touring band's road crew, such as a sound engineer.

clue.text: Busy motorway crossed by adolescent German

indicators.note: crossed by says the motorway runs through the adolescent word

parts.note: a teen is an adolescent
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, written as MI

explanation.surface: A German teenager crossing a busy motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A place teeming with people is crowded and busy.

clue.text: Turning on conservative about independent film's bad reputation

indicators.note: turning says the word on is read the other way round
about says the Tory word goes round the next two pieces

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party
ET is the Spielberg film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: A Conservative turning on an independent film for its bad name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning on' reads like turning against someone, but it only flips the little word 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something bad, an unsavoury reputation.

clue.text: Cartographer parking motor on a hill

indicators.note: in a down clue on says the car sits above the following pieces

parts.note: a Merc is a Mercedes car, a motor
a tor is a rocky hill

explanation.surface: A mapmaker leaving the car on a hillside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parking' just joins the pieces, putting the car on the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerardus Mercator was the Flemish mapmaker behind the Mercator projection.

clue.text: Real pay adjusted around end of June 2020, say

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap round that last letter
adjusted says the letters of real pay are rearranged
the end of June is its last letter

explanation.surface: Real wages reset at the end of June 2020.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adjusted' rearranges REAL PAY, and 'around' puts the E from the end of June inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: 2020 had a 29 February, making it an example of a leap year.

clue.text: Forward female with limp runs after earl

indicators.note: after says the runs letter follows the earl letter

parts.note: lank means limp, as of hair
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A forward woman with a limp running after a nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby a flanker is a forward who plays on the flank of the scrum.

clue.text: Middle class gets behind church trust

indicators.note: gets behind says the class letters come after the others

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
NT is the National Trust, which looks after British historic houses
RE is Religious Education, a school class

explanation.surface: The middle class backing the church and a trust.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, Religious Education, is a school subject in Britain; 'class' means a lesson, not a social class.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre is the middle point of something; it is also a rugby back position.

clue.text: Initially choosing hotel over a rented holiday home

indicators.note: in a down clue over says the hotel letter sits above the rest
initially points to the first letter of choosing

parts.note: Hotel is H in the radio phonetic alphabet
let means rented out

explanation.surface: Choosing a hotel rather than a rented holiday home.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a wooden cabin, often rented by holidaymakers in the mountains.

clue.text: Leave band and record 'Coming Up'

parts.note: ELO is the Electric Light Orchestra

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up says the record letters read upwards

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Quitting the group and releasing a record titled Coming Up.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to leave secretly, usually to marry.

clue.text: Tall story about deserted creek is foul

parts.note: high means tall

indicators.note: about says the story word goes round the remaining letters

parts.note: a tale is a story

indicators.note: a deserted word is emptied of its middle, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A tall tale about an abandoned creek is outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserted' empties the creek of its inner letters; 'is foul' reads as a verdict on the story but 'foul' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A high tackle, above the shoulders, is an illegal challenge in rugby, so a foul.

clue.text: Spirit that is suppressed by dope

indicators.note: in a down clue suppressed by says the abbreviation sits below, held down by the dope word above it

parts.note: gen and dope are both slang for information
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A spirit kept down by drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' suggests drugs but means information, GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A genie is a spirit of Arabian folklore, like the one in Aladdin's lamp.

clue.text: Drag polo horses around 3 points in 14?

indicators.note: to horse around is to fool about, so the letters of drag polo are scrambled

explanation.surface: Polo ponies dragged around the field.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs into 27 Down, GOAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop goal, kicked from a dropped ball, scores three points in rugby, as in the Six Nations.

clue.text: See 26
Jumping contest hooligan hosts in Spain

indicators.note: hosts says the hooligan word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a lout is a hooligan
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A yob putting on a show-jumping event in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A line-out is a rugby restart where forwards jump to contest the thrown-in ball.

clue.text: Part of the ogre regularly given to blue-eyed boy

parts.note: pro means in favour of, given to

indicators.note: part of says only some letters of the words are used
regularly picks every other letter of the ogre

explanation.surface: Some of the ogre's role being handed to a favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' and 'regularly' together take the alternate letters T, E, G, E from 'the ogre'.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue-eyed boy is a favourite, someone promoted by a patron, which is what a protégé is.

clue.text: Attempt to conceal twisted plot involving a government department

indicators.note: to conceal says the attempt word hides the rest inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt, and a rugby score

indicators.note: involving says the jumble takes in the letter a
twisted says the letters of the plot word are rearranged

parts.note: a ruse is a scheme or plot

explanation.surface: An effort to cover up a twisted plot inside a ministry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' rearranges the plot word to RESU before the A goes in; 'Attempt' is also a rugby score, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Treasury is the UK ministry responsible for public finances.

clue.text: Old actor retired in Monterey? Al Pacino!

indicators.note: retired says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the words Monterey? Al Pacino

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Al Pacino in Monterey, now retired from acting.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft left 'in' as a link word, but it is the hiding signal; 'retired' then reads the hidden REYALP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Player is an old-fashioned word for a stage actor, as in Shakespeare's 'all the world's a stage'.
